overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers indexing correspondence and reports on Taiwan’s petroleum industry, principally the discovery of oil in the Kinsui field, recent industry developments, and oil production during the first six months of 1932. The listed items include reports from Taihoku and acknowledgments or commendations from the Navy and Commerce Departments, with particular attention to the value of Consul Ketcham’s reporting.

subfiles.title: Department of State list of papers on the Taiwan petroleum industry
subfiles.about: An index records reports and official correspondence concerning oil discoveries, petroleum-industry developments, and production in Taiwan.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists papers relating to an oil strike in the Kinsui field and to recent developments in Taiwan’s petroleum industry. It also records acknowledgments and favorable comments from the Navy and Commerce Departments, including Captain Ellis’s commendation and the forwarding of material to Consul Ketcham. A final entry concerns a voluntary report on Taiwan’s oil production during the first six months of 1932.

interest: This page is useful as a finding aid because it reconstructs a sequence of petroleum-related reports and interdepartmental responses whose underlying documents are not reproduced here. It shows that commercial and consular reporting from colonial Taiwan circulated among the State, Navy, and Commerce Departments and was judged particularly valuable. It also points historians toward specific subjects—especially the Kinsui oil strike and production in early 1932—and identifies Reed, Ketcham, and Ellis as participants in that reporting network.
